Hopefully, this can help with finding the root cause.
@antiagainst @hanhanW thanks for looking on this issue and suggestions!

The benchmarking tool will try to iterate 10, 100, 1000, 10000... times

https://github.com/google/iree/blob/6bd3b1dc13236566d1f8ee651cd3ab9b03dd8a1d/iree/tools/benchmark_module_main.cc#L137-L149

It works if you break the loop earlier, like right after the 127 iteration, on vulkan.

I count on the iterations, it seems that it can only execute 128 times in the loop.

It looks like it's related to kMaxInFlightFenceCount. If I set it to 64 then it can only iterate 64 times.

https://github.com/google/iree/blob/6bd3b1dc13236566d1f8ee651cd3ab9b03dd8a1d/iree/hal/vulkan/timepoint_util.h#L123
And 256 times if I set the number to 256.
@ScottTodd could you take a look at this?
Can you try with https://github.com/google/iree/pull/2800 ? That would be nice to land, but it's tricky to know for sure if each of the changes in that area are fixing issues without causing more :/
That is working with another change I have. We need to release the input before others. Ie, add `inputs.reset();` after the loop. I'll send out the PR for releasing inputs.
hmm, it just works with my patch. I remembered I tried it this afternoon, but it's not working. Anyway, I'll send out the PR to fix this.
Thanks for looking into it and fixing this, @hanhanW!

Hello, 

It seems the same Vulkan memory leak problem is still in the python binding. The simplest way to reproduce the error is to take [colab's low level invoke example](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/colab/low_level_invoke_function.ipynb). Put everything except the import in an infinite loop. Also, change the driver_name to "vulkan" and run it. 

On my machine with Nvidia P100 GPU, the exception: "Check failed: m_pMetadata->IsEmpty() && "Some allocations were not freed before destruction of this memory block!" always pops up in the iteration 83.
Can it be reproduced in tool level on your machine? Ie, compile the `simple_mul` with `iree-translate` and run on `iree-run-benchmark`.
No, it cannot be reproduced in iree-translate/iree-benchmark-module. Think the issue is specific to the python binding.
Let's move the discussion to #3381, since it only happens on python binding.

```
$ build-android/host/bin/iree-translate \
    -iree-mlir-to-vm-bytecode-module \

    -o /tmp/simple-vulkan.vmfb
```

```
starlte:/data/local/tmp $ ./iree-benchmark-module -driver=vulkan -input_file=simple-vulkan.vmfb -entry_function=abs -inputs="i32=2"
```

@antiagainst can you please share, have you seen this issue?

Forking from #2948, since this is a python binding issue.

@lioujheyu reported that there is a memory leak issue on vulkan in python binding. the error is to take [colab's low level invoke example](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/colab/low_level_invoke_function.ipynb). Put everything except the import in an infinite loop. Also, change the driver_name to "vulkan" and run it.

On his machine with Nvidia P100 GPU, the exception: "Check failed: m_pMetadata->IsEmpty() && "Some allocations were not freed before destruction of this memory block!" always pops up in the iteration 83.

The issue cannot be reproduced in iree-translate/iree-benchmark-module. Think the issue is specific to the python binding.

===

Look into the example doc, I didn't find any import in an infinite loop. @lioujheyu could you post the code?
@ScottTodd could you help on this issue? I'm not familiar with using colab, so would be great if you can take the first round. I'm happy to learn it and debug, thanks!
